claims.summary: At (4,4), W = 2^(-l_1), for N large, deterministically: for every grid function g >= 0 on the mesh W of discrete cost sum_e W^2 psi_4^*(|Delta_e g|/(2W)) at most 2 and every lambda >= 1, with l_s the length of the inner edges e of the boundary of {g > s} whose larger value is at most lambda |Delta_e g| and phi(l) = l (2 log_2(1 + 1/(W l)) + 5)^(3/4), the integral of phi(l_s) over s >= 0 is at most 16 lambda (3.5 + log_2(lambda)/8)^(3/4) sqrt(log N) + C lambda (log log N)^(3/4), C universal.
claims.assessment: Working proof, passed with corrections by one medium reviewer (research/results/ultimate_matching_anchored_increments_20261018/review.txt): dyadic levels a_j = 2^j a_0, a_0 = 2 lambda e^16 W; for s in [a_j, a_(j+1)) the counted edges have larger value above a_j; the first sum, swapped to the edges, charges each edge 2W w_e (2 log_2(1 + w_e/W) + 5)^(3/4) <= 8 lambda cost_e (3.5 + log_2(lambda)/8)^(3/4) (log(v_e/2))^(1/2) through w_e <= lambda W v_e and the psi_4^* lower bound at v_e > 2e^16; the second over at most log_2 N levels of total mass at most 2 lambda T(2).
claims.rationale: The level sum of lem:dyadic-level-sum for every edge whose increment is a fixed fraction of its larger value, not only edges next to the zero set; the full reach of the per-layer route.
claims.next_action: A joint bound for increments that are a small fraction of their larger value (non-anchored), which the per-set charge sqrt(log N) per length cannot give for continuous lower layers (Leighton-Shor, citing Shor's lower bound, unread), up to the transfer to cells.

claims.summary: At (4,4), W = 2^(-l_1), on the events of lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor at the mesh W and of lem:cut-cell-variance-bound at kappa = 1, for N large: for every lambda >= 1, every grid function g on the mesh W of discrete cost at most 2 such that each inner edge whose two cells carry values of one strict sign has max(|g(c)|, |g(c')|) <= lambda |Delta_e g| (edges with Delta_e g = 0 excepted) has |D(g)| <= C lambda (1 + log lambda)^(3/4) sqrt(N log N), C universal.
claims.assessment: Working proof, passed with corrections by one medium reviewer (research/results/ultimate_matching_anchored_increments_20261018/review.txt): g = g^+ - g^-, each nonnegative, of cost at most that of g, and lambda-anchored (an edge where one side is not positive is anchored at lambda = 1); the layer cake over {g > s}; each layer charged by lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (a) when its perimeter is below 1 and lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (b) otherwise, both at most C sqrt N (phi(P) + P sqrt(log N)); TV(g) <= T(2); lem:anchored-level-sum.
claims.rationale: Every function whose nonzero increments are a fixed fraction of the larger adjacent value meets the one-height target's bound, any number of distinct values.
claims.next_action: Non-anchored increments of large multiplicity, first the bunched staircase stack, by a ramp plus step-texture split with Bernstein's inequality and a union over coarse monotone paths; the per-set charge sqrt(log N) per length fails for continuous lower layers by the Leighton-Shor lower bound (cited, unread), up to a transfer to cells.
